In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the precipitation reaction of immune sera can occur with substances of very small molecular weight and that it is determined by chemical composition as well as by colloidal state of solution.
serological precipitation is a phenomenon that is independent of the molecular weight of the reacting substances.
the serological precipitation of a substance is a phenomenon dependent on the molecular constitution of the precipitated substance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the precipitin reactions are not due to the formation of a new substance, but are caused by the combination of antibody with a specific chemical compound.
serological reactions are not restricted to proteins but may take place with substances of small or even of very small molecular weight.
the serological reaction with simple chemical compounds is a precipitation reaction which, like the reaction with bacterial antigens, is determined by the colloidal state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antibody is a protein, but the antigen is not a protein.

the immune sera prepared by injection of azoprotein antigens react with the azodyes, and that these precipitin reactions are not due to the protein component of the antigen but are caused by the azo component.

the immune system is capable of recognizing and binding a wide array of small molecules, including drugs, and that this recognition is specific and can be exploited to detect and measure drugs and drug metabolites in biological fluids.
